mainTopic: Measurements of the מזבח and the אמה, respect for kings, the arrangement of the לחם הפנים, and the direction of the ארון and its poles
overview: The amud opens by finishing a point about the מזבח: its קרנות are measured with the small five-טפח אמה. Adding up the מזבח in טפחים (58 total, 29 half, 23 from the top down to the סובב) shows the סובב is six טפחים above the middle. That fits a ברייתא, and the wording of the פסוק supports it too. The גמרא then sets the medium אמה at six טפחים, proving it from the שלחן. It also explains why the מקדש kept two longer measuring rods in שושן הבירה: so workers would never take הקדש money they had not earned. This leads to why שושן הבירה was pictured on the eastern gate, to the rule of respecting the king, and to the healing leaves of the future river. Next comes a ברייתא showing that every word about the לחם הפנים is needed to teach two rows of six. רבי rules that with rows of seven the top loaf is ignored, because he reads 'על' as 'next to'. Finally, a ברייתא teaches that the ארון lay across the width of the בית, which we know from its poles, and begins explaining how the poles were 'seen' yet 'not seen outside'. That answer comes on the next amud.

steps.title: Corners: height and width use the same small cubit
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its earlier point: for the קרנות, height and width are measured the same way, with the five-טפח אמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes no difference this way, and it makes no difference that way.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is wrapping up an answer it started before this line. For the קרנות of the מזבח, height and width are both measured with the five-טפח אמה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Other parts of the מזבח use a large six-טפח אמה, but the יסוד and the קרנות use the small five-טפח one. Here the גמרא adds that for the קרנות there is no split between height and width. This is the number the next calculation depends on.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes no difference; the rule is the same
This way (here: height and width)

phrases.english: It makes no difference this way
phrases.notes: This means the height of the קרנות.

phrases.english: and it makes no difference that way.
phrases.notes: And this means their width. Both use the five-טפח אמה.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא שְׁנָא הָכִי וְלָא שְׁנָא הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends an answer from the discussion just before this line
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The קרנות are measured with the five-טפח אמה in both height and width.

steps.title: Adding up the altar in handbreadths
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finds the full height of the מזבח, its halfway point, and the distance from the top of the קרנות down to the סובב.
steps.simpleTranslation: How tall is the מזבח? Fifty-eight טפחים. How much is half the מזבח? Twenty-nine. How much is it from the קרנות down to the סובב? Twenty-three.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא works out three numbers, one after another, by asking a quick question and answering it each time. It is setting up a comparison in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מזבח is ten אמות tall. Eight of them are six-טפח אמות and two (the יסוד and the קרנות) are five-טפח אמות: 48 + 10 = 58, so half is 29. From the top of the קרנות to the סובב is 5 (the קרנות) plus three six-טפח אמות (18), which is 23.

keyTerms.meaning: The outer altar
Its half
The raised corners on top of the altar
The ledge running around the altar

phrases.english: How much is the altar?
phrases.notes: He means its height, counted in טפחים.

phrases.english: Fifty-eight.
How much is half of the altar?
Twenty-nine.
From the corners until the surrounding ledge, how much is it?
Twenty-three.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the five-טפח קרנות from step 1 in the arithmetic
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Altar = 58 טפחים; half = 29; top of the קרנות to the סובב = 23.

steps.title: The ledge is six handbreadths above the halfway mark, which fits a ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The distance from the top down to the סובב is six less than half, so the סובב is six טפחים above the halfway line. That explains a ברייתא that allows the service a full אמה below the כהן's feet.
steps.simpleTranslation: How much short of half the מזבח is it? Six. And we learned: if he did it below his feet, even one אמה, it is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא compares 23 with 29 and gets a gap of six טפחים. It then shows that this gap matches a ruling we already know.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the סובב is six טפחים above the halfway point, a כהן standing on the סובב can go down a whole אמה and still be in the upper half of the מזבח. That is exactly why the ברייתא says doing it an אמה below his feet is still valid. The math explains the ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: Less than; short of
Below his feet (below where the כהן stands on the סובב)
Valid

steps.confusionAlert: 'Six' here is not the height of anything. It is the gap between 29 (half the מזבח) and 23 (top down to the סובב), which shows how far the סובב sits above the middle.

phrases.english: How much is it short of half the altar?
phrases.notes: He is comparing 23 against 29.

phrases.english: Six.
And we learned: If he performed it below his feet,
even one cubit, it is valid.
phrases.notes: An אמה below the סובב is still above the halfway line, so it still counts as the upper part.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the result from step 2's numbers and ties it to a ברייתא
steps.raayaObject: That the סובב is six טפחים above the halfway point of the מזבח
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא: if done below his feet, even one אמה, it is valid
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the measuring system (five-טפח קרנות and יסוד) fits a known ruling about where on the מזבח the service may be done.

steps.title: The verse's wording supports this reading
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק uses two different phrases, 'חיק האמה' and 'אמה רחב', which supports measuring the parts of the מזבח differently.
steps.simpleTranslation: The wording is exact too, since it is written 'the bottom shall be an אמה' and 'an אמה wide.' Learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds support from the wording of the פסוק and then closes the point with שמע מינה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says 'חיק האמה' about the יסוד and 'אמה רחב' (width) about the סובב. Because only the second phrase mentions width, the first must be about height. So the יסוד's אמה is a height, and the סובב's אמה is a width, which fits the calculation the גמרא has been using.

keyTerms.meaning: The wording is also exact (it backs this up)
The 'bottom' of the altar, one אמה
Width
Learn from this; it is proven

steps.whatToRemember: The סובב is six טפחים above the middle of the מזבח (58 total, 29 half, 23 from the top down to the סובב). That is why the service may be done even an אמה below the סובב, and the פסוק's wording supports this.

phrases.english: It is also precise,
as it is written: "The bottom shall be a cubit"
phrases.notes: יחזקאל 43:13

phrases.english: and "a cubit the breadth,"
Conclude from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds support from the פסוק after the support from the ברייתא
steps.raayaObject: That the parts of the מזבח are measured differently
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The measuring scheme is supported by both the ברייתא and the wording of the פסוק.

steps.title: How many handbreadths is a medium cubit?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how big an אמה בינונית is.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how many טפחים is a medium אמה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a simple measuring question: how many טפחים make up the 'medium' אמה? This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, רבי מאיר said most אמות in the מקדש were medium-sized אמות. Before going further, the גמרא wants that size pinned down as a number.

keyTerms.meaning: A medium cubit, the standard middle-sized אמה
Handbreadths, the smaller unit used to measure an אמה

phrases.english: And how much is a medium cubit?
phrases.notes: This goes back to רבי מאיר's view on 97a, that most אמות in the מקדש were medium ones.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the מזבח's measurements to defining the basic medium אמה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The size of an אמה בינונית in טפחים.

steps.title: A medium cubit is six handbreadths
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers that a medium אמה is six טפחים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: six טפחים.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives the answer: a medium אמה is six טפחים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This sets the baseline number. Everything that follows, the proof and the bigger אמות, is measured against six טפחים.

keyTerms.meaning: Six

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan says:
Six handbreadths.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: An אמה בינונית equals six טפחים.

steps.title: Support from the measurements of the שלחן
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי בר אבין proves the six-טפחים answer from רבי מאיר's measurement of the שלחן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי בר אבין said: We also learned this in a משנה. רבי מאיר says: the שלחן is twelve טפחים long and six wide.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי בר אבין brings a משנה that backs up רבי יוחנן's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה says the שלחן was two אמות long and one אמה wide. רבי מאיר says it was twelve טפחים by six, so each אמה must be six טפחים. That matches רבי יוחנן exactly.

keyTerms.meaning: We also learned it, meaning a משנה supports this
The Table in the משכן and the מקדש

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei bar Avin says:
We also learned this in a mishna:
Rabbi Meir says:
The Table, its length is twelve handbreadths,
phrases.notes: The תורה says the Table was two אמות long and one wide (שמות 25:23), so twelve and six means six per אמה.

phrases.english: and its width is six.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי יוחנן's answer with a משנה.
steps.raayaObject: That an אמה בינונית is six טפחים.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי מאיר's measurement of the שלחן, twelve by six טפחים, compared with the פסוק's two by one אמות.

steps.title: Does 'medium' imply a bigger cubit exists?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether calling it 'medium' means there is also a larger אמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Can we learn from this that there is an אמה bigger than it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notices the word 'medium' and asks whether that means a bigger אמה exists. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Something is called 'medium' only if there are sizes above and below it. So the גמרא checks whether a larger אמה was really in use.

keyTerms.meaning: From the implication of, meaning can we infer
That is larger than it

phrases.english: Does this imply that there is a cubit
that is larger than it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a question out of the word 'medium' used in steps 5 to 7.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether an אמה larger than six טפחים existed.

steps.title: Yes: the two cubits in שושן הבירה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers yes and quotes a משנה about two longer measuring rods kept in שושן הבירה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes. As we learned in a משנה: There were two אמות in שושן הבירה, one on the northeast corner and one on the southeast corner. The northeast one was half an אצבע longer than משה's אמה. The southeast one was half an אצבע longer than that one. So it was a full אצבע longer than משה's אמה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says yes, bigger אמות existed, and proves it from a משנה about two measuring rods in the מקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: משה's אמה is the six-טפחים one. One rod was half an אצבע longer than it, and the other was a full אצבע longer. So there really were אמות larger than the medium one.

keyTerms.meaning: Shushan the capital, a chamber above the eastern gate of the הר הבית
משה's cubit, the standard six-טפחים אמה
Fingerbreadth, a small unit of measure
Longer by, more than

phrases.english: Yes, and so we learned in a mishna:
There were two cubit-rods in Shushan the capital,
phrases.notes: This was a room over the eastern gate of the הר הבית, where the measuring rods were kept.

phrases.english: one on the northeast corner
and one on the southeast corner.
The one on the northeast corner

phrases.aramaic: יְתֵירָה עַל שֶׁל מֹשֶׁה חֲצִי אֶצְבַּע,
phrases.english: was longer than Moses' cubit by half a fingerbreadth,
the one on the southeast corner
was longer than that one by half a fingerbreadth,

phrases.aramaic: נִמְצֵאת יְתֵירָה עַל שֶׁל מֹשֶׁה אֶצְבַּע.
phrases.english: so it turns out to be longer than Moses' cubit by a full fingerbreadth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 8 with a yes and proves it from a משנה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes. There were אמות half an אצבע and a full אצבע longer than משה's six-טפחים אמה.

steps.title: Why have a large and a small measure?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה asks why the חכמים wanted both a larger and a smaller אמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why did they say there should be one large and one small?
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה itself asks why two sizes of אמה were needed. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Having measures of different sizes looks confusing, so the משנה explains what the extra length was for.

keyTerms.meaning: Large
Small

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'small' means the regular אמה, which is משה's six-טפחים one, and 'large' means a longer rod from שושן הבירה. The 'small' one is not smaller than six טפחים.

phrases.english: And why did they say
one large and one small?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָמָה אָמְרוּ אַחַת גְּדוֹלָה וְאַחַת קְטַנָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same משנה by asking why the different sizes existed.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The purpose of keeping a larger and a smaller אמה.

steps.title: So workers never misuse Temple property
steps.stepSummary: Workers were paid by the small measure and delivered work by the large one, so they never committed מעילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: So that the craftsmen would take payment by the small measure and give back work by the large measure, so that they would not come to מעילה.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה explains that the two sizes protected the workers from accidentally taking הקדש money they had not earned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Pay was counted by the smaller אמה, but the work had to measure up by the larger אמה. So the workers always gave a little more than they were paid for. That way they never ended up with extra הקדש money, which would be מעילה.

keyTerms.meaning: Craftsmen, artisans
Misusing הקדש, Temple property, for personal benefit
They take, here meaning their pay
They give back, here meaning delivering the finished work

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how carefully the חכמים guarded הקדש. They built in a safety margin so that no worker would ever be paid too much.

phrases.english: So that the artisans would
take payment by the small one,
and return it by the large one,
so that they would not come to misuse consecrated property.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The extra length is a safety margin so that workers are never overpaid from הקדש.

steps.title: Why two large cubits?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why two different larger אמות were needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why do I need two?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why there were two longer rods when one would seem to be enough. This sets up its final answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the only goal is a safety margin, one longer rod should do the job. So why keep two, one half an אצבע longer and one a full אצבע longer?

keyTerms.meaning: Why do I need two?

phrases.english: And why do I need two?
phrases.notes: He means the two longer rods in שושן הבירה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the reason in step 11 and asks why that reason needs two larger rods.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why two separate larger אמות were kept.

steps.title: One for silver and gold, one for building
steps.stepSummary: The shorter extra rod was for silver and gold work, and the longer one was for construction.
steps.simpleTranslation: One was for silver and gold, and one was for building.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that each larger rod had its own job: one for precious metals and one for construction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Silver and gold are expensive, so the margin there was only half an אצבע, which keeps the workers from losing too much. For ordinary building, a margin of a full אצבע was used.

keyTerms.meaning: Silver and gold
Building, construction

steps.whatToRemember: An אמה בינונית, which is משה's אמה, is six טפחים. The מקדש also kept two longer rods, half an אצבע and a full אצבע longer. Workers were paid by the smaller measure and delivered work by the larger one to avoid מעילה. The half-אצבע rod was for silver and gold, and the full-אצבע rod was for building.

phrases.english: One for silver and gold,
and one for building.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 12 and closes the discussion of the larger אמות.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Each larger rod had a separate use: the half-אצבע rod for silver and gold, and the full-אצבע rod for construction.

steps.title: Why was שושן הבירה pictured on the eastern gate?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה that the eastern gate of the הר הבית had a picture of שושן הבירה on it, and asks why.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in a משנה elsewhere: the eastern gate had a picture of שושן הבירה on it. What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a related משנה about שושן הבירה and asks why its picture was on a gate of the הר הבית. This sets up the next step, where two answers are given.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier steps mentioned measuring rods kept in שושן הבירה. Now the גמרא connects to another place where שושן הבירה shows up: a picture on the Temple Mount gate. It is strange to put a picture of a Persian capital on a gate of the holy place, so the גמרא wants the reason.

keyTerms.meaning: The eastern gate of the הר הבית
Shushan the capital, the royal city of the Persian kings
A picture or image
What is the reason?

phrases.english: We learned there:
phrases.notes: This is a משנה in מדות 1:3.

phrases.english: The eastern gate,
upon it Shushan the capital was depicted.
What is the reason?

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן הָתָם: שַׁעַר הַמִּזְרָח, עָלָיו שׁוּשַׁן הַבִּירָה צוּרָה. מַאי טַעְמָא?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the measuring rods kept in שושן הבירה to another משנה that mentions שושן הבירה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why a picture of the Persian capital was placed on a gate of the הר הבית.

steps.title: Two reasons for the picture of שושן
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא and רב יצחק בר אבדימי disagree: one says it reminded the people where they came from, the other says it kept the fear of the kingdom upon them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא and רב יצחק בר אבדימי: one said it was so they would know where they came from, and one said it was so the fear of the kingdom would be upon them.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים give two different reasons for the picture. We are not told which אמורא said which reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Reason one is about memory and thankfulness: the people returned to ירושלים from the Persian empire, so the picture reminded them of that. Reason two is about respect for the government: seeing the Persian capital kept them in awe of the king so they would not rebel.

keyTerms.meaning: One said... and one said (a dispute where we don't know who said which)
From where they came
Fear and respect for the ruling kingdom

steps.confusionAlert: Don't try to match the opinions to the names. The גמרא uses 'חד אמר... וחד אמר' exactly because it does not say who held which view.

phrases.aramaic: רַב חִסְדָּא וְרַב יִצְחָק בַּר אַבְדִּימִי,
phrases.english: Rav Ḥisda and Rav Yitzḥak bar Avdimi:
One said:
so that they would know from where they came,
phrases.notes: He means they'd remember that they came back to ירושלים from the Persian empire.

phrases.english: and one said:
so that the fear of the kingdom would be upon them.

steps.triggerLanguage: חַד אָמַר: כְּדֵי שֶׁיֵּדְעוּ מֵהֵיכָן בָּאוּ, וְחַד אָמַר: כְּדֵי שֶׁתְּהֵא אֵימַת מַלְכוּת עֲלֵיהֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Either to remember they came from Persia, or to keep the fear of the Persian kingdom upon them.

steps.title: Always respect the king: משה and פרעה
steps.stepSummary: רבי ינאי teaches that one should always fear the kingdom, proven from משה speaking respectfully to פרעה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ינאי said: The fear of the kingdom should always be upon you, as it says, 'All these servants of yours will come down to me and bow to me, saying...' But he did not say this about פרעה himself.
steps.whatsHappening: Picking up on the idea of אימת מלכות from the second opinion, רבי ינאי teaches it as a general rule and brings a פסוק as proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the end, פרעה himself came running to משה at night. Yet when warning him, משה only said that פרעה's servants would come and bow. He avoided saying it about פרעה himself out of respect for a king, even a wicked one.

keyTerms.meaning: Always
Whereas about him himself
He did not say it to him

steps.whyThisMatters: This turns the reason given for the picture into a lasting rule of behavior: show respect to rulers, even when they don't deserve it.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yannai says:
The fear of the kingdom should always be upon you,
as it is stated:
“And all these, your servants, shall come down to me,
phrases.notes: שמות 11:8. משה is talking to פרעה.

phrases.english: and bow down to me, saying”,
whereas about himself he did not say it to him.
phrases.notes: פרעה himself ended up coming too, but משה didn't say that to his face.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יַנַּאי: לְעוֹלָם תְּהֵא אֵימַת מַלְכוּת עָלֶיךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands the second reason of step 15 (אימת מלכות) into a general rule with a source.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person should always show fear and respect toward the ruling power.

steps.title: A different source: אליהו runs before אחאב
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן learns the same rule of respecting the king from אליהו running before אחאב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: From here, as it says, 'The hand of ה׳ was on אליהו, and he tied up his belt and ran before אחאב until the entrance of יזרעאל.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן agrees with the rule but brings a different פסוק to prove it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אחאב was a wicked king, and אליהו was a great נביא. Still, אליהו ran in front of אחאב's chariot like a servant honoring the king, which shows that a king must be respected.

keyTerms.meaning: From here (a different source)
He tied up his belt (got ready to run)

steps.whatToRemember: Both רבי ינאי and רבי יוחנן teach אימת מלכות: respect for the king. They only differ in the source: משה and פרעה, or אליהו and אחאב.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said: From here,
as it is stated:
“And the hand of the Lord was on Elijah,
phrases.notes: מלכים א 18:46.

phrases.english: and he girded up his loins,
and ran before Ahab
to the entrance of Jezreel.”

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an alternative source for the same rule taught by רבי ינאי in step 16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The rule of respecting the king is learned from אליהו running before אחאב.

steps.title: What the healing leaves will open
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא and רב יצחק בר אבדימי disagree about which 'mouth' the leaves of the future river will open: the actual mouth or the womb.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And its leaf for healing' (לתרופה): רב חסדא and רב יצחק בר אבדימי disagree. One said it means to open the mouth above. The other said it means to open the mouth below.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another disagreement between the same two sages from the earlier step. This one is about the word לתרופה in a פסוק in יחזקאל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word לתרופה is read as two words joined together: להתיר פה, 'to open the mouth.' The two sages agree on that reading. They only disagree about which 'mouth' is meant. One says the real mouth, so the mute will speak. The other says the womb, so barren women will have children.

keyTerms.meaning: healing; here read as a joined form of לְהַתִּיר פֶּה
to open (unlock) the mouth
the 'upper mouth': the actual mouth used for speaking
the 'lower mouth': the womb

steps.confusionAlert: Both sides agree that לתרופה means 'opening a mouth.' The only argument is which mouth.

phrases.english: "And its leaf for healing"
phrases.notes: יחזקאל 47:12. The word לתרופה is being read as להתיר פה, 'to open the mouth.'

phrases.aramaic: רַב חִסְדָּא וְרַב יִצְחָק בַּר אַבְדִּימִי,
phrases.english: Rav Chisda and Rav Yitzchak bar Avdimi [disagree]:
One said: to open the mouth that is above,
and one said: to open the mouth that is below.
phrases.notes: The 'mouth below' is the womb, so barren women would be able to give birth.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעָלֵהוּ לִתְרוּפָה רַב חִסְדָּא וְרַב יִצְחָק בַּר אַבְדִּימִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another disagreement between the same pair of sages, on a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: לתרופה means להתיר פה. One view says it opens the mouth of the mute; the other says it opens the womb of the barren.

steps.title: Another pair of sages holds the same two views
steps.stepSummary: חזקיה says the leaves open the mouths of the mute. בר קפרא says they open the wombs of barren women.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also stated: חזקיה said it means to open the mouth of the mute. בר קפרא said it means to open the 'mouth' of barren women.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the same disagreement also appears between חזקיה and בר קפרא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the two views are spelled out clearly. 'Upper mouth' means the mute will speak, and 'lower mouth' means barren women will give birth. This also tells us these were two well-known readings held by more than one pair of sages.

keyTerms.meaning: people who cannot speak
women who cannot have children

steps.whatToRemember: The healing leaves 'open a mouth.' That means either curing the mute or helping barren women have children.

phrases.english: It was also stated:
Chizkiya said: to open the mouth of the mute;

phrases.aramaic: בַּר קַפָּרָא אָמַר לְהַתִּיר פֶּה עֲקָרוֹת.
phrases.english: Bar Kappara said: to open the "mouth" of barren women.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְּמַר חִזְקִיָּה אָמַר לְהַתִּיר פֶּה אִלְּמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a matching disagreement that spells out the two sides of step 18.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חזקיה: the leaves cure the mute. בר קפרא: the leaves cure barren women.

steps.title: Why the Torah adds 'six in a row'
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא explains that 'twelve loaves in two rows' alone could mean uneven rows of four and eight. So the Torah adds 'six.'
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: Suppose the Torah had only said, 'Take fine flour and bake twelve loaves, and place them in two rows,' and had not said 'six.' I would have said one row could have four and the other eight. That is why it says 'six.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new topic, the לחם הפנים. It brings a ברייתא explaining why the Torah needed the words 'six in a row.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Knowing 'twelve loaves' and 'two rows' does not tell us the rows must be equal. Twelve could be split four and eight. The word 'six' makes each row exactly six.

keyTerms.meaning: the twelve loaves placed on the שולחן in the מקדש
a row or stack of loaves
loaves (cakes)
had it been written: a way of testing what a פסוק would mean without some of its words
I would have said: the mistaken reading we would have had
that is why it says: the extra words are there to block the mistake

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: Had it said:
"And you shall take fine flour and bake it
twelve loaves
and you shall place them in two rows"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 24:5–6

phrases.english: and had it not said "six,"
I would have said:

phrases.aramaic: אַחַת שֶׁל אַרְבַּע וְאַחַת שֶׁל שְׁמוֹנֶה,
phrases.english: one [row] of four and one of eight.
Therefore it says "six."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic: the arrangement of the לחם הפנים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The word 'six' requires each of the two rows to hold exactly six loaves.

steps.title: Why the Torah adds 'twelve'
steps.stepSummary: Without 'twelve,' one might think there could be three rows of six. So the Torah fixes the total at twelve.
steps.simpleTranslation: And suppose the Torah had only said, 'Two rows, six in a row,' and had not said 'twelve.' I would have said there could be three rows of six each. That is why it says 'twelve.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues. It shows that the number 'twelve' is also needed, to block a different mistake.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without the total, 'six in a row' might be read as a rule for every row. Then one might think more rows of six could be added, such as three rows. 'Twelve' caps the total, so there are exactly two rows of six. Each number in the פסוק closes a gap the other leaves open.

keyTerms.meaning: six in each row
twelve: the total number of loaves

steps.whatToRemember: The לחם הפנים is exactly two rows of six. 'Six' rules out uneven rows, and 'twelve' rules out extra rows. Neither number is extra.

phrases.english: And had it said:
"Two rows, six in a row,"
and had it not said "twelve,"

phrases.aramaic: הָיִיתִי אוֹמֵר שָׁלֹשׁ שֶׁל שֵׁשׁ שֵׁשׁ,
phrases.english: I would have said: three [rows] of six each.
Therefore it says "twelve."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִילּוּ נֶאֱמַר שְׁתַּיִם מַעֲרָכוֹת שֵׁשׁ הַמַּעֲרָכֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The second half of the same ברייתא: it now explains why 'twelve' is needed, after explaining 'six.'
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The word 'twelve' limits the לחם הפנים to exactly two rows of six, with no extra rows.

steps.title: Without 'two' and 'six,' one might think of three rows of four
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא gives its last possibility: if the Torah had only said 'twelve' and 'rows,' one could make three rows of four. That is why the Torah also says 'two' and 'six.'
steps.simpleTranslation: If the Torah had said only 'twelve loaves' and 'rows,' without 'two' and 'six,' I would have said to make three rows of four loaves each. That is why it says 'two' rows and 'six' in a row.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes its list of wrong setups. Each one is ruled out by a different word in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 20 used 'six' to rule out rows of four and eight. Step 21 used 'twelve' to rule out three rows of six. Here 'two' and 'six' rule out three even rows of four, so every word in the פסוק has a job.

keyTerms.meaning: Rows or stacks of the לחם הפנים on the שולחן
Four each, meaning every row has four loaves

phrases.english: And had it said 'twelve loaves' and 'rows,'
phrases.notes: These words come from ויקרא 24:5-6.

phrases.english: but had it not said 'two' and 'six,'

phrases.aramaic: הָיִיתִי אוֹמֵר שָׁלֹשׁ שֶׁל אַרְבַּע אַרְבַּע,
phrases.english: I would have said three rows of four loaves each.
That is why it says 'two' and 'six.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Third and final 'had it said only...' case in the same ברייתא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The words 'two' and 'six' rule out three rows of four.

steps.title: All three phrases are needed
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא concludes that we could only learn the correct arrangement once all three phrases were said.
steps.simpleTranslation: So until these three phrases in the פסוקים were said, we could not have learned it.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא sums up its derivation. None of the words in the פסוק is extra.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each phrase alone leaves room for a wrong setup. Only 'twelve,' 'two rows,' and 'six in a row' together lock in exactly two rows of six.

keyTerms.meaning: Phrases or words of the פסוק
We could not have learned it

steps.whatToRemember: The לחם הפנים must be two rows of six, and the Torah needs all three phrases (twelve, two, six) to teach this.

phrases.english: So until there were said
these three phrases, we could not learn it.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא עַד שֶׁלֹּא יֵאָמְרוּ שְׁלֹשָׁה מִקְרָאוֹת הַלָּלוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Wraps up the three cases of the ברייתא
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: All three phrases together are needed to teach two rows of six.

steps.title: The practical rule: two rows of six, not four and eight
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא states the practical law: the כהן places two rows of six. If he made one row of four and one of eight, he has not fulfilled the מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: How is it done? He places two rows of six each. If he placed one row of four and one of eight, he has not fulfilled his obligation.
steps.whatsHappening: Now that the source is clear, the ברייתא gives the practical instructions and one invalid case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The derivation becomes a strict rule. Uneven rows, even with the right total of twelve, do not count.

keyTerms.meaning: How is this done? This opens the practical rule
He has not fulfilled his obligation

phrases.english: How is it done?

phrases.aramaic: נוֹתֵן שְׁתַּיִם מַעֲרָכוֹת שֶׁל שֵׁשׁ שֵׁשׁ,
phrases.english: He places two rows of six each.
And if he placed one row of four
and one of eight, he has not fulfilled his obligation.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא כֵּיצַד? נוֹתֵן שְׁתַּיִם מַעֲרָכוֹת שֶׁל שֵׁשׁ שֵׁשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the derivation as a practical law
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two rows of six are required. Four and eight is invalid.

steps.title: רבי: with rows of seven, ignore the top loaf
steps.stepSummary: If there were two rows of seven, רבי says we view the top loaf of each row as if it is not there, so the setup is valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: If there were two rows of seven each, רבי says: we look at the top loaf as if it is not there.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא brings a case with too many loaves, and רבי rules that the extra loaf on top is simply ignored.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike four and eight, the rows of six are still complete here. The extra loaf sits on top, so רבי treats it as not part of the row.

keyTerms.meaning: We view it, meaning we treat it as
The top loaf
As if it is not there

phrases.english: Two rows of seven each:
רבי says: we view the top loaf
as if it is not there.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁתַּיִם שֶׁל שֶׁבַע שֶׁבַע, רַבִּי אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a case of extra loaves to the rule of two rows of six
steps.mimraCoreRuling: With rows of seven, the top loaf is ignored and the setup is valid.

steps.title: But the לבונה must be placed 'on' the row
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי: the פסוק says the לבונה must be put 'על' the row. An extra loaf on top would block it from the real row.
steps.simpleTranslation: But don't we need 'and you shall place on'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי's ruling from step 25 using the פסוק about the לבונה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'על' means right on top, the לבונה would sit on the extra seventh loaf, not on the six real loaves. So how can רבי say it is valid?

keyTerms.meaning: But don't we need? This opens a challenge
And you shall place on. The פסוק about putting the לבונה on the row

phrases.english: But don't we need 'and you shall place on'?
phrases.notes: ויקרא 24:7. The לבונה is supposed to go 'on' each row of loaves.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי's ruling
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי's ruling that the top seventh loaf is ignored
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If 'על' means directly on top, the extra loaf stands between the לבונה and the real loaves.

steps.title: רבי holds that 'על' means 'next to'
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא and רב המנונא answer that רבי follows his own view: 'על' means 'next to,' so the לבונה does not have to touch the loaves.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said to רב המנונא, and some say רב המנונא said to רב חסדא: רבי follows his own reasoning, since he said 'על' means 'next to.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. רבי is just being consistent with how he reads the word 'על'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the לבונה only needs to be next to the row, an extra loaf on top blocks nothing. So the challenge falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: Following his own reasoning, meaning consistent with his view elsewhere
Next to, close by

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב חִסְדָּא לְרַב הַמְנוּנָא,
phrases.english: רב חסדא said to רב המנונא,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרִי לַהּ רַב הַמְנוּנָא לְרַב חִסְדָּא:
phrases.english: and some say רב המנונא said it to רב חסדא:
רבי follows his own reasoning,
since he said 'על' means 'next to.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the key word of the פסוק according to the speaker's own known view
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'על' means directly on top, so the extra loaf would block the לבונה
steps.terutzMaskana: For רבי, 'על' means next to, so the extra loaf is no problem
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רבי is saying the לבונה can go anywhere. He is only saying it is enough for it to be next to the row; it does not have to sit directly on the loaves.

steps.title: Proof from the פרוכת that 'על' can mean 'next to'
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that רבי reads 'על' as 'next to,' and proves it from the פסוק about the פרוכת, which hung next to the ארון, not on top of it.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: רבי says, 'and you shall place on the row pure לבונה' means next to. Do you say 'על' means next to, or does it really mean right on top? When it says 'and you shall screen the ארון with the פרוכת,' you must say 'על' means next to.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to prove that רבי really does hold this view, and that the Torah uses 'על' this way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פרוכת was a curtain hanging in front of the ארון, not lying on it. Since the Torah still uses 'על' there, the word can mean 'next to.'

keyTerms.meaning: Pure frankincense, placed with the לחם הפנים
Really on, directly on top
The curtain in front of the קודש הקדשים
You must say. This introduces the forced conclusion

steps.whyThisMatters: This one proof backs up רבי's ruling about rows of seven. It also teaches a reading of 'על' that can be used in other places.

phrases.english: As it was taught: רבי says,
'And you shall place on the row pure frankincense':
phrases.notes: ויקרא 24:7

phrases.english: 'on' means next to.
You say 'on' means next to,
or perhaps it means nothing but really on top?

phrases.aramaic: כְּשֶׁהוּא אוֹמֵר ״וְסַכֹּתָ עַל הָאָרֹן אֶת הַפָּרֹכֶת״,
phrases.english: When it says 'and you shall screen the Ark with the Curtain,'
phrases.notes: שמות 40:3. The curtain hung in front of the ארון, not on top of it.

phrases.english: you must say 'on' means next to.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: רַבִּי אוֹמֵר ״וְנָתַתָּ עַל הַמַּעֲרֶכֶת לְבֹנָה זַכָּה״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proves the claim made in the answer
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא of רבי, using the פסוק of the פרוכת and the ארון (שמות 40:3)

steps.title: Direction of the כלים in the מקדש; the ארון is the exception
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה. A ברייתא teaches that all the כלים lay along the length of the בית, except the ארון, which lay along its width. It then adds a line about the ארון's poles, which the next steps explain.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: all the vessels in the מקדש, etc. The Rabbis taught: all the vessels in the מקדש had their length along the length of the House, except the ארון, whose length was along the width of the House. That is how it was placed, and that is how its poles were placed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting the next line of the משנה, then brings a ברייתא that explains it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא adds an exception the משנה did not spell out: the ארון faced the other way, across the width of the בית. Its last line about the poles is unclear, so the גמרא asks about it in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: The vessels of the מקדש, such as the שולחן, מנורה, and מזבח
The length of the House, from east to west
The width of the House, from north to south
The poles used to carry the ארון

steps.whatToRemember: All the כלים ran east to west along the length of the בית. Only the ארון ran north to south, across the width. Its poles ran east to west, and steps 30-31 show that this is how we know the ארון's direction.

phrases.english: All the vessels in the Temple, etc.
The Rabbis taught: all the vessels in the Temple
had their length along the length of the House,

phrases.aramaic: חוּץ מֵאָרוֹן שֶׁאׇרְכּוֹ לְרׇחְבּוֹ שֶׁל בַּיִת,
phrases.english: except the Ark, whose length was along the width of the House.
And that is how it was placed,
and that is how its poles were placed.

steps.triggerLanguage: כׇּל הַכֵּלִים שֶׁבַּמִּקְדָּשׁ וְכוּ׳. תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the משנה to begin a new topic
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All the כלים lay along the length of the בית, except the ארון, which lay along the width.

steps.title: What does the last line of the ברייתא mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the ברייתא means by its last line about the ארון and its poles.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the ברייתא saying?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops on the last line of the ברייתא from the previous step because its meaning is unclear. This question sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said the ארון lay across the width of the בית, and then added a line about its poles. It is not clear how the poles connect to the ארון's direction, so the גמרא asks for an explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: What is it saying? A request to explain unclear wording

phrases.english: What is it saying?
phrases.notes: He means the last line of the ברייתא from the step before: 'and its poles were placed that way.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of the last clause of the ברייתא quoted in step 29.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the line about the poles connects to the statement that the ארון lay across the width of the בית.

steps.title: We know how the ארון lay from the direction of its poles
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא means: we know the ארון lay across the width of the בית because of the way its poles were placed.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what it is saying: the ארון was placed that way (across the width), and we know this from the way its poles were placed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that the ברייתא's last line is giving a proof. The direction of the poles shows us the direction of the ארון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The poles ran east to west, along the length of the בית, pointing toward the פרוכת. Because of how the poles were attached to the ארון, poles facing that way mean the ארון itself had to lie across the width of the בית. So the line about the poles is the source, not just an extra fact.

keyTerms.meaning: The poles used to carry the ארון
Placed, lying

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read the ברייתא as saying the poles lay the same way as the ארון. The poles ran along the length of the בית (east to west), and that is what proves the ארון lay across the width.

phrases.english: This is what it is saying:
In this way the ארון was placed,
phrases.notes: 'In this way' means across the width of the בית, as the ברייתא said.

phrases.english: as we know from the fact that its poles were placed in that way.
phrases.notes: The poles pointed east to west, along the length of the בית.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 30 by reading the last clause as a proof.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The poles' east-west direction proves the ארון lay across the width of the בית.

steps.title: How do we know which way the poles faced?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that the poles ran east to west.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how do we know the direction of its poles?
steps.whatsHappening: Now that the ארון's direction depends on the poles, the גמרא asks how we know the poles ran east to west. This sets up the ברייתא that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof in step 31 only works if we are sure about the poles. So the גמרא asks for a source for that piece.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know this?

phrases.english: And its poles, how do we know?
phrases.notes: He means: how do we know the poles faced east to west, toward the פרוכת?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the fact that step 31 relied on.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that the poles of the ארון ran east to west.

steps.title: The poles reached the פרוכת, because the פסוק says they were seen
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא reads the פסוק 'the poles were long' and says they touched the פרוכת, because the פסוק says their ends 'were seen.'
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: 'And the poles were long.' You might think they did not touch the פרוכת. So the פסוק says 'and they were seen.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא on a פסוק in מלכים to show that the poles stretched toward the פרוכת. First it proves the poles reached all the way to the פרוכת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the poles were short, nobody outside the קדש הקדשים could see any sign of them. Since the פסוק says their ends 'were seen' from the היכל, they must have reached the פרוכת. That means they pointed east, toward the פרוכת.

keyTerms.meaning: And the poles were long (מלכים א 8:8)
The curtain between the היכל and the קדש הקדשים
You might have thought
So the פסוק teaches

phrases.english: As it is taught: 'And the poles were long' –
phrases.notes: מלכים א 8:8.

phrases.english: You might think they did not touch the curtain?
So the verse says: 'And they were seen.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering step 32 with a ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The words 'and they were seen' show the poles reached the פרוכת, so they pointed toward it, east to west.

steps.title: The poles did not tear through the פרוכת
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא adds that the poles did not break through the פרוכת, because the פסוק says 'they were not seen outside.'
steps.simpleTranslation: If it says 'they were seen,' you might think the poles tore through the פרוכת and stuck out. So the פסוק says: 'They were not seen outside.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues and blocks the opposite mistake: maybe the poles poked right through the פרוכת. The second half of the פסוק rules that out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the פסוק seems to say two opposite things: the poles 'were seen,' yet 'were not seen outside.' The ברייתא uses each half to block a wrong idea: one says the poles reached the פרוכת, the other says they did not tear through it.

keyTerms.meaning: Tearing through
They were not seen outside

phrases.english: If only 'and they were seen' –
you might think they tear through the curtain and come out?
So the verse says: 'They were not seen outside.'
phrases.notes: This is the end of the same פסוק, מלכים א 8:8.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא, limiting what step 33 learned from 'and they were seen.'
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The poles did not break through the פרוכת into the היכל.

steps.title: How can both halves of the פסוק be true?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks how the poles can be both 'seen' and 'not seen outside.'
steps.simpleTranslation: How can this be?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks how to fit together the two halves of the פסוק. This is a setup question; the answer comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 33 showed the poles reached the פרוכת, and step 34 showed they did not tear through it. The ברייתא now needs a picture where both are true at once.

keyTerms.meaning: How can this be? A call to reconcile two sources

steps.whatToRemember: The poles of the ארון pointed east to west toward the פרוכת. The פסוק teaches they reached the פרוכת but did not break through it, and this is how we know the ארון lay across the width of the בית.

phrases.english: How can this be?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises the tension between the two halves of the פסוק used in steps 33 and 34.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the poles could be seen from the היכל and yet not come out through the פרוכת.
